questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place that holds many different experiences combined with high academic standards.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved a lot of welcome and information letters along with instructions on how to set up my student ID, student pass, my courses etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The only thing that was a bit frustrating, was the lack of information about the availabilty on courses. The units were difficult to find, and a lot of the units were not created or already fully occupied. For example did the univeristy enrol me in a unit that they later denied me from because the unit only welcomed students ooutside EU. This resulted in my having some changing courses that I did not find as interesting as my initial wishes.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is easy and social and much closer to the campus in the centre, than the on campus sites.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an email and an invitation to an on campus enrolment.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails, phonenumber, Monash Abroad team and on campus help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. All of my first wishes for classes were dismissed due to the units not being created. Then I enrolled in a unit which Monash accepted and later I found out that I did not qualify to take the class. Then i had to switch classes again. But I did enjoy my last classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be openminded and ready for a different way of teaching, learning and taking the exams.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were a lot heavier than on UCPH. I think it was because I only took research units on post graduate level. The level was estimated to be a 7.5 ECTS class, but the exams and readings were equivalent to a 15 ECTS. It was very interesting and high level of teaching and researching.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was very different as the teaching included class participation, different kinds of exams (tests, research articles and reflection paper). The only thing that was the same was the potential class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Explore the city, the coastline and other cities nearby!! Also Uluru to see some ancient history and learn about aboriginal culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be openminded
Explore the resturants and culture
Invest your time in friends to do roadtrips and other adventures together

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at options for classes and have some plan B classes ready if something does not goes to plan

questions.answer: The learning outcome and cultural difference by living in a much bigger city.
